statement: Given positive integers $m$ and $n$. Let $a_{i,j}$ ($1\leq i\leq m$, $1\leq j\leq n$) be non-negative real numbers with $a_{i,1}\geq a_{i,2}\geq\cdots\geq a_{i,n}$ and $a_{1,j}\geq a_{2,j}\geq\cdots\geq a_{m,j}$. Let $X_{i,j}=a_{1,j}+\cdots+a_{i-1,j}+a_{i,j}+a_{i,j-1}+\cdots+a_{i,1}$ and $Y_{i,j}=a_{m,j}+\cdots+a_{i+1,j}+a_{i,j}+a_{i,j+1}+\cdots+a_{i,n}$. Prove that $\prod_{i=1}^m\prod_{j=1}^n X_{i,j}\geq\prod_{i=1}^m\prod_{j=1}^n Y_{i,j}$.

Given positive integers $n$ and $k$, $n>k^2>4$. In an $n\times n$ grid, a $k$-group is a set of $k$ unit squares in different rows and different columns. Determine the maximal $N$ such that one can choose $N$ unit squares and color them, so that in any $k$-group from the colored squares, there are two of the same color and two of different colors.

Given positive integer $n$. Prove that for any integers $a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_n$, at least $\lceil\frac{n(n-6)}{19}\rceil$ numbers from $\{1,2,\ldots,\frac{n(n-1)}{2}\}$ cannot be represented as $a_i-a_j$ ($1\leq i,j\leq n$).

Let $f(x),g(x)$ be polynomials with integer coefficients. If for infinitely many primes $p$ there exists an integer $m_p$ such that $f(a)\equiv g(a+m_p)\pmod{p}$ for all $a\in\mathbb{Z}$, prove that there exists a rational $r$ with $f(x)=g(x+r)$.

Given triangle $ABC$, a circle $\Omega$ tangent to $AB$ and $AC$ at $B$ and $C$ respectively. $D$ is the midpoint of $AC$, $O$ is the circumcenter of $ABC$. A circle $\Gamma$ through $A,C$ intersects the minor arc $BC$ on $\Omega$ at $P$ and $AB$ at $Q$. The midpoint $R$ of minor arc $PQ$ satisfies $CR\perp AB$. Ray $PQ$ meets $AC$ at $L$, $M$ is the midpoint of $AL$, $N$ is the midpoint of $DR$, $X$ is the projection of $M$ onto $ON$. Prove the circumcircle of $\triangle DNX$ passes through the center of $\Gamma$.

Given positive integer $n$ and $r$ pairwise distinct primes $p_1,\ldots,p_r$. Initially the $(n+1)^r$ numbers $p_1^{i_1}\cdots p_r^{i_r}$ ($0\leq i_1,\ldots,i_r\leq n$) are on the blackboard. Alice (gcd) and Bob (lcm) alternate moves; Alice goes first. The game ends when one number remains. Find the minimal $M$ such that Alice can guarantee the remaining number is $\leq M$.

Cyclic quadrilateral $ABCD$ has $AB+BC=AD+DC$. Let $E$ be the midpoint of arc $BCD$, $F$ ($\neq C$) the antipode of $A$. Let $I,J,K$ be the incenter of $\triangle ABC$, the $A$-excenter of $\triangle ABC$, and the incenter of $\triangle BCD$. If $\triangle BIC\overset{+}{\sim}\triangle KPJ$, prove $EK$ and $PF$ meet on the circumcircle.

Given positive integers $n,k$ with $n\geq 2$. Find the minimum constant $c$ such that: for any positive integer $m$ and $kn$-regular graph $G$ with $m$ vertices, one can color the vertices with $n$ colors so that the number of monochromatic edges is at most $cm$.

Given positive integers $a,b,c$ pairwise coprime. Let $f(n)$ be the number of non-negative integer solutions $(x,y,z)$ to $ax+by+cz=n$. Prove there exist $\alpha,\beta,\gamma\in\mathbb{R}$ such that $|f(n)-(\alpha n^2+\beta n+\gamma)|<\frac{1}{12}(a+b+c)$ for all non-negative integers $n$.
Find all functions $f:\mathbb{Z}^+\to\mathbb{Z}^+$ such that for all positive integers $m,n$ with $m\geq n$: $f(m\varphi(n^3))=f(m)\cdot\varphi(n^3)$, where $\varphi$ is Euler's totient function.

Let $n$ be a positive integer and $a_1,\ldots,a_{2n+1}$ positive reals. For $k=1,\ldots,2n+1$, let $b_k=\max_{0\leq m\leq n}\frac{1}{2m+1}\sum_{i=k-m}^{k+m}a_i$ (indices mod $2n+1$). Prove that the number of $k$ with $b_k\geq 1$ is at most $2\sum_{i=1}^{2n+1}a_i$.

Find the smallest positive real $a$ such that for any three points $A,B,C$ on the unit circle, there exists an equilateral triangle $PQR$ with side length $a$ such that all of $A,B,C$ lie on the interior or boundary of $\triangle PQR$.

Given positive integer $n\geq 5$ and a convex polygon $P=A_1A_2\cdots A_n$ with no three diagonals concurrent. Prove one can choose a point inside every quadrilateral $A_iA_jA_kA_l$ ($1\leq i<j<k<l\leq n$) not on any diagonal, such that the $\binom{n}{4}$ points are distinct and any segment connecting two of them intersects some diagonal of $P$.

Given distinct positive integers $a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_{2020}$. For $n\geq 2021$, $a_n$ is the smallest number different from $a_1,\ldots,a_{n-1}$ that does not divide $a_{n-2020}\cdots a_{n-1}$. Prove every sufficiently large number appears in the sequence.
Determine the greatest real $C$ such that for every $n\geq 2$ there exist $x_1,\ldots,x_n\in[-1,1]$ with $\prod_{1\leq i<j\leq n}(x_i-x_j)\geq C^{n(n-1)/2}$.

Prove that $\sum_{m=1}^n 5^{\omega(m)}\leq\sum_{k=1}^n\lfloor n/k\rfloor\tau(k)^2\leq\sum_{m=1}^n 5^{\Omega(m)}$, where $\omega(m)$ is the number of distinct prime factors and $\Omega(m)$ counts with multiplicity.
Determine all $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ such that $f(xf(y)+y^3)=yf(x)+f(y)^3$.

Prove there exists a constant $\lambda$ such that for any positive integer $m\geq 2$ and any lattice triangle $T$ containing exactly one $m$-lattice point in its interior (not on the boundary), the area of $T$ is at most $\lambda m^3$. (An $m$-lattice point has both coordinates divisible by $m$.)

Let $n\geq 2$ be a positive integer. Find the minimum $m$ such that there exist $x_{ij}$ ($1\leq i,j\leq n$) satisfying: (1) for every $i,j$, $x_{ij}=\max\{x_{i1},\ldots,x_{ij}\}$ or $x_{ij}=\max\{x_{1j},\ldots,x_{ij}\}$; (2) for every $i$, at most $m$ indices $k$ have $x_{ik}=\max\{x_{i1},\ldots,x_{ik}\}$; (3) for every $j$, at most $m$ indices $k$ have $x_{kj}=\max\{x_{1j},\ldots,x_{kj}\}$.

Triangle $ABC$ ($AB<AC$) with incenter $I$ and circumcircle $O$. Let $M,N$ be midpoints of arcs $\widehat{BAC}$ and $\widehat{BC}$. $D$ on $O$ with $AD\parallel BC$, $E$ tangency point of $A$-excircle. $F$ in $\triangle ABC$ with $FI\parallel BC$ and $\angle BAF=\angle EAC$. Extend $NF$ to meet $O$ at $G$; extend $AG$ to meet line $IF$ at $L$. Lines $AF$ and $DI$ meet at $K$. Prove $ML\perp NK$.

Find all positive integers $n\geq 2$ and rationals $\beta\in(0,1)$ such that there exist positive integers $a_1,\ldots,a_n$ with $S\!\left(\sum_{i\in I}a_i\right)=\beta\sum_{i\in I}S(a_i)$ for every $I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ with $|I|\geq 2$, where $S(n)$ is the digit sum.
Suppose $x_1,\ldots,x_{60}\in[-1,1]$ with $x_{i+60}=x_i$. Find the maximum of $\sum_{i=1}^{60}x_i^2(x_{i+1}-x_{i-1})$.

Find the smallest real $\alpha$ such that for any convex polygon $P$ with area 1, there exists a point $M$ such that the area of the convex hull of $P\cup Q$ is at most $\alpha$, where $Q$ is the image of $P$ under central symmetry with respect to $M$.

Let $n\geq 2$ be an integer. $2n^2$ contestants play a round-robin tournament. Given: (1) if $A$ beats $B$ and $B$ beats $C$, then $A$ beats $C$; (2) at most $\frac{n^3}{16}$ draws. Prove one can choose $n^2$ contestants labeled $P_{ij}$ ($1\leq i,j\leq n$) such that for any $i<i'$, $P_{ij}$ beats $P_{i'j'}$.
